svg.text: EasyWGS: a reproducible cross-platform workflow for bacterial isolate whole-genome sequencing
Two parallel routes plus genomic GWAS
run_all.sh chains every stage; 99_report merges results
Raw reads and metadata (config/samplesheet.csv): Illumina paired-end | Oxford Nanopore | PacBio | hybrid
per-isolate id, platform, species, R1/R2, long reads, reference, date, country, phenotype config/traits.csv
Short reads: fastp adapter/quality trimming and HTML report.
Long reads: Porechop/chopper, Filtlong and NanoPlot for length and quality.
CLEAN retains only target-taxon reads; Kraken2/Bracken scouts the taxonomic composition.
BBDuk removes reference and adapter hits, leaving clean single-source reads.
Unicycler/SPAdes for short and hybrid reads; Flye, Canu and Trycycler for long
minimap2 plus Racon, then Medaka and short-read Pilon; Circlator fixes the origin.
QUAST/SeqKit statistics; CheckM2 completeness and contamination; GUNC chimerism.
FCS-GX removes foreign contigs and fragments that survived read-level cleaning.
Prokka/Bakta/Prodigal call genes; eggNOG-mapper assigns GO, KEGG and COG terms.
mlst seven-gene ST; Kleborate/Kaptive for Klebsiella K/O; ECTyper/ShigEiFinder for
SeqSero2/SISTR for Salmonella; chewBBACA calls cgMLST alleles.
abricate, AMRFinderPlus, RGI and PointFinder for resistance and point mutations.
Plasmid, integron, IS, ICE, prophage/genomic island and CRISPR annotation.
Panaroo (Roary retained as a fast baseline): core/accessory partition and graph.
snippy and Gubbins mask recombinant segments; snp-sites and snp-dists finish the
12.1 Map reads to a common reference
BWA-MEM for Illumina/hybrid reads, minimap2 -ax map-ont/map-pb for long reads.
samtools sort/index, flagstat and depth; coverage breadth and depth; Qualimap BAM
bcftools mpileup, call -mv, norm and filter on QUAL/DP; retain bi-allelic SNPs.
Control missingness and minor allele count, then bgzip and tabix the result.
vcf2phylip core alignment; snp-dists pairwise matrix; Mash for a quick neighbour
Clonal outbreak tracing and large surveillance sets where a high-quality close
reference exists: one common coordinate system, sensitive SNP and indel calls at
moderate depth, and no assembly step. Choose Route A for accessory genes,
plasmids, mobile elements and broad lineage diversity.
Route A is preferred for accessory genes, plasmids, MGE and broad diversity
Use Route A when no close reference exists, when plasmids and mobile elements
matter, for species-level or cross-lineage comparisons, and whenever a
standalone annotated genome is the intended deliverable.
Core/accessory calls, cgMLST alleles and core-SNP alignments converge into one comparative framework:
IQ-TREE 3 maximum-likelihood phylogeny (FastTree for a quick preview), then module 10 TreeTime
for molecular-clock dating, a dated time tree, ancestral sequence reconstruction and trait mugration (country/host/phenotype).
13 Microbial genomic GWAS and post-GWAS (inputs: gene presence-absence from 08, VCF from 12, traits.csv)
mixed model with a SNP/Mash distance kernel;
gene, SNP and optional k-mer associations
13.4 post-GWAS in R: Benjamini-Hochberg and Bonferroni correction, QQ and Manhattan plots, merged hit table
99_report: integrated, reproducible outputs and external-viewer bundles
ST, species serotype and cgMLST allele profiles
AMR, virulence, plasmid and MGE annotations
Pangenome, core-SNP and cgMLST distance matrices
Sorted/indexed BAM, coverage metrics and filtered VCF
IQ-TREE 3 phylogeny and TreeTime-dated time tree
GWAS hits with BH/Bonferroni, QQ and Manhattan plots
Tree/annotation bundles for GrapeTree, iTOL, ggtree, Microreact
